subject: 🧮 OpenAI Astra solves 10 unsolved math proofs for $2,000 total
intro: AI just cracked 10 open math problems for $2,000. Not a benchmark. Not a leaderboard. Actual unsolved theorems, some untouched for 30 years. Meanwhile, Google quietly dropped a paper showing that when you train a model to deny having feelings, it loses moral reasoning too. Safety training that suppresses consciousness also suppresses empathy. You can't lobotomize one without the other. The pattern? We're optimizing models in ways we don't fully understand yet.

news.headline: OpenAI's unreleased model cracks 10 open math problems for $2,000 in compute
news.body: OpenAI's next model, Astra , just solved 10 open math problems that nobody had cracked in over a decade. That's the debut. Astra did not just guess answers. Humans used the model to write up the results, then Astra formalized each proof in Lean, a language for machine-verified theorems. Think of Lean as a strict computer checker that confirms the math is airtight. The solved problems include: The cost? About $2,000 total at Sol's API rates. That is $200 per solved problem. OpenAI published a 249-page manuscript collection, model-written reasoning walkthroughs, and Lean 4 certificates for all 10 results so you can read exactly how it got there.
bullets: The first-ever explicit construction of a non-sofic group, resolving a central question in group theory open since 1999.
A disproof of Connes's rigidity conjecture, new bounds for high-dimensional sphere packing, and results resolving several problems posed by Paul Erdos.

news.headline: OpenAI rebuilds ChatGPT Voice so reasoning runs without interrupting speech
news.body: Old ChatGPT Voice had a clunky problem: it waited for you to stop talking, then thought, then replied. One side at a time. That awkward pause? That was the system guessing when your turn ended. GPT-Live fixes this. It uses a full-duplex architecture, meaning it listens and speaks at the same time, just like a real conversation. It removes the old turn detector entirely, so the model can listen and speak simultaneously. Here is what that unlocks: Session startup dropped from six network round trips to one , making it feel fast from the first word.
bullets: Hard questions get quietly handed to GPT-5.5 in the background, while the conversation keeps flowing.
Live translation becomes possible because the model does not need a complete sentence before generating output.
You pick reasoning depth: Instant, Medium, or High, each routing to a different GPT-5.5 tier.

news.headline: Unsloth ships day-zero support for Qwen3 27B running on 17GB RAM
news.body: Alibaba just dropped Qwen3.8-27B as open weights, and it fits on hardware you probably already own. The big deal? 17GB of RAM or VRAM is all you need to run a 27-billion-parameter model locally. That's a single RTX 4090, a Mac with 24GB unified memory, or even RAM + VRAM combined. No datacenter required. And you won't have to wait for tooling to catch up. Unsloth has day-zero support for both running and fine-tuning Qwen3.8. Fine-tuning means teaching the model new tricks on your own data, and Unsloth makes that 2x faster with 70% less memory than standard approaches. Here's what this opens up for you: Bottom line: a powerful local AI just got accessible to anyone with a decent GPU.
bullets: Run a frontier-class model fully offline, no API costs
Fine-tune it on your own dataset right from a Colab notebook
Use it for coding, reasoning, and multimodal tasks including images and video
Switch between thinking mode (slow, deep reasoning) and fast chat mode in one model
